title: FRT Runner Completion
description: A runner's signed report of what it actually executed for a claimed FRT EXECUTE run. Posted to POST /engine/v1/frt/runs/{runId}/complete. The control plane verifies the attestation before trusting any field; an unverified completion can never mark customerCodeExecuted or productionOperationExecuted as true, and a completion never certifies anything.

expectedVersion.description: Optimistic-concurrency version of the run as last read by the runner. Must equal the stored version or the completion is rejected with a version conflict.

signature.description: Ed25519 signature, base64url, over the canonical JSON of the enclosing object with its own signature field removed. Canonical JSON is defined as: object keys sorted ascending, no insignificant whitespace, and raw UTF-8 rather than \uXXXX escapes. The TypeScript control plane sorts by UTF-16 code unit and Python by code point; these agree for every ASCII key, and all key patterns in this schema are ASCII-only, so no key may be widened beyond ASCII without fixing both implementations in one change.

runnerId.description: Must equal the identity subject completing the run and the executor named on every reported evidence item.

exitStatus.description: FAILED is a real, recorded outcome, not an error: the run lands in FAILED with outcome RUNNER_EXECUTION_FAILED and stays retryable.

customerCodeExecuted.description: True only if the runner really built, ran or tested customer code. Ignored unless the attestation verifies.

productionOperationExecuted.description: True only if the runner really performed a production operation. Ignored unless the attestation verifies.

artifacts.description: Content-addressed outputs the runner produced. Names must be unique; a duplicate name or a missing digest blocks the run.

evidence.description: Evidence the runner produced. The runner is the executor and may never be the verifier.

keyId.description: Must resolve in the trust store to a key carrying the RUNNER purpose.

role.description: Evidence role such as SOURCE_BUILD, TARGET_BUILD, TYPECHECK or NEGATIVE_TEST. A role may appear at most once per completion.

uri.description: Must resolve below an approved evidence root and match byteCount and digest exactly.

state.description: NOT_RUN and INCONCLUSIVE never pass a gate.

verifier.description: Must differ from executor and from runnerId. A runner verifying its own evidence blocks the run.

synthetic.description: Synthetic evidence is recorded but can never support a real gate.
